cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Subscription – a regular payment to access a service or content.

p.em: Example: Many platforms now use subscription models instead of free access.

cosy-blockquote.p: Personalization – adapting a service to fit individual preferences.

p.em: Example: Personalization improves user experience on social media.

cosy-blockquote.p: Privacy – the right to control personal data and information.

p.em: Example: Privacy concerns are growing on digital platforms.

cosy-blockquote.p: Revenue – money a company earns from its business activities.

p.em: Example: Advertising is a major source of revenue for Meta.

cosy-blockquote.p: Creator – someone who produces online content such as videos or posts.

p.em: Example: Many creators depend on social media income.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bot – an automated account or program that performs online actions.

p.em: Example: Bots are often used for spam or fake engagement.

cosy-blockquote.p: Customization – changing features to match personal needs or taste.

p.em: Example: Customization lets users design their profiles.

cosy-blockquote.p: Innovation – the development of new ideas or technologies.

p.em: Example: AI is driving innovation in the tech industry.

cosy-blockquote.p: Engagement – interaction between users and online content.

p.em: Example: Higher engagement increases visibility of posts.

cosy-blockquote.p: Digital divide – the gap between people with and without access to technology.

p.em: Example: Paid AI tools may widen the digital divide.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
A: Private user data is harvested and is processed by network algorithms without consent.B: Subscription models ensure data is protected and kept private.
★ Would you pay for a monthly subscription to your favorite social platform?

A: Paying for service gives users more control over content personalization. B: Public algorithms provide a shared cultural experience rather than isolated, hyper-filtered bubbles.
★ Do you enjoy platform algorithms that guess your tastes, or do you prefer zero personalization?

A: Subscription models offer strict user privacy and zero data-harvesting. B: Free networks are fine as long as they warn users about standard data privacy rules.
★ How much do you actively worry about your online privacy?

A: Direct subscription fee revenue keeps companies focused on improving product quality. B: Advertising revenue allows platforms to stay free and scale up their services.
★ Do you think tech companies earn too much revenue from selling user data?

A: Platforms can share subscription revenue directly with each verified content creator. B: Creator programs on free platforms allow anyone to gain viral fame without initial fees.
★ Have you ever financially supported an independent content creator?

A: Charging a fee makes it expensive for spam operations to run an automated bot army. B: Free access is essential, even if it means dealing with the occasional malicious bot.
★ How often do you spot an automated bot while browsing social networks?

A: Premium subscriptions allow deep UI customization and an ad-free experience. B: Standardized, simple designs are easier to navigate and keep everyone on equal footing.
★ Is visual customization of your device or apps important to you?

A: Direct funding from users fuels faster software innovation and updates. B: Advertising budgets have historically funded the grandest technological innovation projects.
★ What is the most exciting technological innovation you have seen recently?

A: Subscription features increase authentic engagement by filtering out low-quality comments. B: Free systems maximize general user engagement and democratic public debate.
★ How has your level of social media engagement changed over the years?

A: Paid platforms can fund digital literacy classes, helping to close the digital divide. B: Charging a fee directly widens the digital divide by locking out low-income users.
★ Do you see a widening digital divide in your city or country?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
A: Monthly subscription fees can drain a student's budget, leading to digital isolation. B: Free platforms force users to pay with their attention, which is worse than a subscription.
★ How many digital subscription services do you currently pay for?

A: Relying on extreme personalization can feed conspiracy theories and divide communities. B: Zero personalization results in a chaotic, irrelevant feed that bores users.
★ Have you ever felt that platform personalization was trapping you in an echo chamber?

A: Tech giants might still sell user data secretly, violating their paid privacy promises. B: Ad-supported models treat user privacy as a secondary commodity.
★ Do you trust big tech corporations to protect your digital privacy?

A: If subscription revenue drops, platforms might compromise their ethics to survive. B: Relying solely on ad revenue incentivizes clickbait headlines and fake news.
★ Do you think clickbait is ruined by the obsession with ad revenue?

A: A paid system might only reward the most famous creator, leaving small channels with nothing. B: Ad-revenue models on free platforms offer a creator highly unpredictable and tiny payments.
★ If you were a content creator, would you prefer subscriptions or ad shares?

A: Spammers might still pay to run a sophisticated bot network on premium sites. B: Free networks are easily overwhelmed by fake bot reviews and accounts.
★ Do you think a social network can ever be 100% free of any automated bot?

A: Endless options for customization can complicate apps, confusing older users. B: A total lack of customization makes modern apps feel rigid and outdated.
★ Do you find complex app settings and customization menus annoying?

A: Monopolies have no incentive to focus on innovation, even with paid users. B: Ad-revenue models promote psychological manipulation instead of genuine product innovation.
★ Do you think the tech industry is slowing down in terms of real innovation?

A: Lower overall engagement occurs when paid walls separate friends and families. B: Relentless fight for ad engagement results in toxic online arguments and outrage.
★ Have you ever deleted a social media app because of toxic engagement?

A: Paid subscriptions create a clear class system, widening the digital divide. B: Standard free ad models ignore the digital divide, leaving vulnerable users with poor security.
★ How can society bridge the digital divide for low-income families?

ul.li: Incorrect: I'm not agree with paying → Correct: I don't agree with paying ((Agree is a verb))
Incorrect: The most of people use WhatsApp → Correct: Most people use WhatsApp ((Generalization))
Incorrect: It depends of the revenue model → Correct: It depends on the revenue model ((Depends on))
Incorrect: I am using Facebook since ten years → Correct: I have been using Facebook for ten years ((Present Perfect Continuous))

Incorrect: I saw a very interesting information on Instagram → Correct: I saw some very interesting information / a very interesting piece of information on Instagram ((The word 'information' is uncountable and cannot be preceded by the indefinite article 'a'))
